⚜️ 12 January: the veneration of the icon of the Mother of God “the Nursing Mother” (Galaktotrophousa)
◘ The Galaktotrophousa icon (the Nursing Mother, the Nourisher of Life) shows the fully human nature of the Saviour without overlooking the divine one... It also shows unfathomable humility: the Child Saviour receives food like any other child
◘ The icon I am showing you today (model: workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, second half of the 19th century) shows the Mother of God holding the Child Jesus in His mature aspect (Emmanuel). Jesus Christ Emmanuel is shown as a child with some features of a grown man, such as the broad forehead, which reflects His divine wisdom
◘ The icon, painted on glass (22x26 cm) in the traditional technique (egg-emulsion tempera and gold leaf), is not available; it was made to order
b0dd3070b599:
◘ Over time, the icon of the Mother of God “the Nursing Mother” (Galaktotrophousa) has been made (on wood or on glass) in various versions. One of the oldest such depictions of the Mother of God is on the Holy Mountain of Athos (Hilandar Monastery); other depictions of this theme (as miniatures) can be admired in manuscripts and (of course) many delightful depictions are found in the icons on glass of the Transylvanian icon painters
◘ The icon on this theme (model: workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, second half of the 19th century) was painted on glass in our workshop; this icon is venerated every year on 12 January
◘ Today I am showing you the drawing of the icon (in ink, with a calligraphy pen)

69e997071a5f:
⚜️ On 4 September the icon of the Mother of God “the Burning Bush” is celebrated

• « The Mother of God and the “Burning Bush” » – icon painted on glass, modelled on several depictions, one of them being the first icon on this theme to reach our country, at the venerable foundation of Saint Antim the Iberian, the Antim Monastery in Bucharest, in the 1940s.

• Many generations of the Church's servants and of the faithful have prayed before this icon, and it also inspired the well-known hesychast movement “The Burning Bush”, a group that kept the fire of faith alive in the hearts of many Romanians, especially during the communist rule.

• According to the painters' manual, the icon “The Burning Bush” shows a large eight-pointed star in the form of overlapping rhombuses, with the Mother of God holding the Saviour in her arms at their centre. Four of the eight points are red, representing the fire, and the other four, coloured green, symbolise that the bush did not burn but remained whole.

• On the points of the red star are the symbols of the four Holy Evangelists: the angel (Saint Matthew), the lion (Saint Mark), the ox (Saint Luke) and the eagle (Saint John), and on the four points of the green star the Holy Angels are depicted.

• If you would like a similar icon, contact me and we will settle the details. This icon is not available; it was made to order.

• This icon is one of the five I have painted in our workshop. I chose the one I am showing you today at random.
